llm_findings.summary: Changing `>= 100` to `> 100` silently removes the discount for orders exactly at 100
llm_findings.explanation: The comparison operator was changed from inclusive to exclusive. As a result, an order_total of exactly 100.0 (and any value that compares equal to 100, including 100.0 arrived at via floating-point arithmetic) now falls into the no-discount branch, whereas it previously received the discount. This is an off-by-one boundary change whose correctness depends on the business rule for the threshold; if the requirement is 'orders of 100 or more qualify', this is a logic regression. Note that the type is float, so values like 99.99999999999999 will also behave differently at the edge.
llm_findings.suggested_fix: If the threshold is meant to be inclusive, restore `if order_total >= 100:`. If excluding exactly 100 is intentional, document the threshold semantics and add a boundary test at 100.0 (and just below/above) to lock in the intended behavior.
